$comment: The catalog's texts in English (components.json has them in Japanese): the same ids. Studio shows these to a page in English (Catalog.InEnglish). Every title, note and description of components.json has its English here (CatalogTests).

noneOption.title: No support
noneOption.description: What .NET does not have is stubbed to compile (it throws when run); what it has stays as it is (its exceptions and differences too). Listed in the conversion report

compat.title: Compatible (Response.End's abort undone)
compat.description: Thread.ResetAbort is replaced with Platform.ResetAbort: the code after the catch runs as on .NET Framework

none.title: No support
none.description: ResetAbort throws (a 503 in the catch after a redirect, for one)

compat.title: Compatible (run on the thread pool)
compat.description: BeginInvoke / EndInvoke are replaced with FrameworkOnCore.AsyncDelegate

compat-package.title: Compatibility package
compat-package.description: System.Runtime.Serialization.Formatters and EnableUnsafeBinaryFormatterSerialization. Existing data can be read. Reading untrusted data is dangerous (as on .NET Framework)

framework.title: As .NET Framework (the ANSI code page)
framework.description: Encoding.Default is replaced with Platform.DefaultEncoding (Windows: the OS's setting; Linux: LANG's culture)

none.title: As .NET (UTF-8)
none.description: The bytes of files and hashes may differ from .NET Framework's

framework.title: As .NET Framework
framework.description: Doubles and floats made text (ToString, concatenation, interpolation, string.Format, Convert.ToString, Append and Write) go through FrameworkNumbers; Parse, TryParse and TimeSpan.From* through FrameworkParsing. FrameworkOnCore's System.Web writes bound values the same way

none.title: As .NET
none.description: 0.1 + 0.2 is 0.30000000000000004, -0 is "-0", 2.675 as N2 is 2.67; parsing a number too large gives infinity

translations.title: FrameworkOnCore's translations
translations.description: System.Web's texts (Calendar's titles, Login's labels, Wizard's and GridView's buttons, error pages) in FrameworkOnCore's own translations (the repository's translations/, MIT), for the languages the original server had a language pack for (capture-culture.ps1 records them; else this machine's). The wording may differ from Microsoft's

framework.title: Microsoft's language packs (Windows only)
framework.description: Satellites made from this machine's .NET Framework language packs (the original server's wording). Microsoft's license forbids distributing them to run on another platform than Windows: only when not deployed on Linux (--deploy none). Microsoft's license terms apply to the deployment

register.title: Registered (always)
register.description: FrameworkOnCore's System.Web (UseWebForms) registers CodePagesEncodingProvider at start: Shift_JIS, EUC-JP and the others are there

stderr.title: Standard error on Linux
stderr.description: The event log on Windows; on Linux, the service's journal or the container's log (FrameworkOnCore.EventLogs)

compat.title: Compatible (no account outside Windows)
compat.description: WindowsIdentity.GetCurrent and the others are replaced with Platform's

ef6.title: Move to EF6
ef6.description: Adds Entity Framework 6's package, rewrites the namespaces, embeds the EDMX

compat.title: Compatible (works on Windows only)
compat.description: Directory/File.GetAccessControl and the others go to FrameworkOnCore.DirectoryAcl and FileAcl (they throw on Linux)

port.title: The port (Windows and Linux)
port.description: FrameworkOnCore's System.Drawing.Common (package FrameworkOnCore.Drawing.Common, from dotnet/runtime 6.0's source: GDI+ on Windows, libgdiplus on Linux; the deployment installs libgdiplus and fonts). FrameworkOnCore's System.Web depends on it: every application has it

port.title: Use the port
port.description: System.Data.Linq ported from referencesource (MIT): package FrameworkOnCore.Data.Linq

none.title: No support
none.description: Stubbed. DLLs that reference it (System.Web.Mvc's model binding) throw too

retarget.title: Retarget
retarget.description: The types a DLL without source references as "assembly + type" that .NET 10 has in another assembly (CallContext in FrameworkOnCore's System.Web): the converter retargets the DLL's references to them. Members the type lacks are replaced with calls of the compatibility assembly's extension members. The DLL works as it is (the rewritten DLLs are in the output's foc-retargeted)

none.title: No support
none.description: The DLL stays as it is: where it uses those types or members, it throws TypeLoadException or MissingMethodException at run time

port.title: Use the port
port.description: FrameworkOnCore's System.Data.SqlClient (package FrameworkOnCore.Data.SqlClient, from dotnet/maintenance-packages 4.9.0's source). It expands |DataDirectory| in connection strings to App_Data as .NET Framework does, and takes Asynchronous Processing, Network Library and Connection Reset, which .NET rejects (SqlConnectionStringBuilder has the properties of those names too). The web project always has it: Entity Framework's connections and the DLLs' are its

dotnet.title: Use .NET's
dotnet.description: Microsoft's System.Data.SqlClient package (4.9.0). A connection string built in code with |DataDirectory| throws (the runtime expands the configuration's). Connection strings with Asynchronous Processing, Network Library or Connection Reset throw too

port.title: Use the port
port.description: System.Web.DataVisualization ported from referencesource (MIT): package FrameworkOnCore.Web.DataVisualization (drawn with the ported System.Drawing: it works on Linux too)

port.title: Use the port
port.description: System.Web.Mobile ported from referencesource (MIT): package FrameworkOnCore.Web.Mobile (MobilePage, the mobile: controls, the device adapters)

none.title: No support
none.description: Stubbed (mobile pages throw). A using alone is removed

corewcf.title: Run on CoreWCF
corewcf.description: The site's .svc services and web.config's system.serviceModel run on CoreWCF within the application (package FrameworkOnCore.ServiceModel): basicHttpBinding, basicHttpsBinding, wsHttpBinding, webHttpBinding (REST), WCF 4's default endpoints and behaviors, serviceActivations, WSDL. The service-side types (ServiceBehavior, WebGet) are rewritten to CoreWCF's. ASP.NET AJAX's enableWebScript too (ScriptManager's ServiceReference, Service.svc/js). Not netTcpBinding, custom ServiceHostFactory, aspNetCompatibilityEnabled (HttpContext.Current in an operation)

none.title: No support
none.description: The services do not run (.svc answers 404). The service-side types are stubbed

insensitive.title: Case-insensitive, as on Windows
insensitive.description: The deployment has casefs (libfoccase.so), which start.sh loads

sensitive.title: Case-sensitive (as Linux is)
sensitive.description: A file the application names in another case is not found

iis.title: As IIS
iis.description: Written as IIS writes it: its format, fields and file names (u_exYYMMDD.log). When writing falls behind, requests wait (no line is dropped). The original server's logFile settings apply

aspnetcore.title: ASP.NET Core's W3C log
aspnetcore.description: ASP.NET Core's W3CLogger. Its format differs a little from IIS's (no sc-substatus), and it writes up to a limit. It stays as it is once the application is rewritten for ASP.NET Core

off.title: Off
off.description: No request log (a load balancer's in front, say)

iis.title: As IIS
iis.description: The rules run as IIS's URL Rewrite module runs them (inheritance, server variables, Wildcard, the query string's order, redirects' absolute URLs). The original server's globalRules too

aspnetcore.title: ASP.NET Core's Rewriter
aspnetcore.description: ASP.NET Core's rewriting (AddIISUrlRewrite): the root web.config only, some differences from IIS, and the application does not start with rules it cannot read (subStatusCode, Wildcard, some server variables)

iis.title: As IIS
iis.description: Error answers are replaced as IIS replaces them (errorMode, existingResponse, File, ExecuteURL, Redirect). IIS's own pages are simple ones

aspnetcore.title: ASP.NET Core's status code pages
aspnetcore.description: A short text for an error without a body. The application's answers are not replaced

off.title: Off
off.description: An error without a body stays empty

iis.title: As IIS
iis.description: Compressed as the original server's static and dynamic compression are set (without its settings, Windows' defaults: a static file gzipped from its second request within 10 seconds)

aspnetcore.title: ASP.NET Core's ResponseCompression
aspnetcore.description: Every answer of the types compressed (brotli first; not over HTTPS by default)

off.title: Off
off.description: Left to a load balancer or CDN in front

thread-abort.title: Thread abort (Thread.Abort / ResetAbort)
thread-abort.note: Converter: ResetAbort is replaced with Platform.ResetAbort (it undoes the abort of Response.End in FrameworkOnCore's System.Web). Abort is not supported

async-delegates.title: Asynchronous delegate calls (BeginInvoke / EndInvoke)
async-delegates.note: Converter: replaced with FrameworkOnCore.AsyncDelegate (run on the thread pool)

binary-formatter.title: BinaryFormatter / SoapFormatter
binary-formatter.note: Converter: the compatibility package System.Runtime.Serialization.Formatters and EnableUnsafeBinaryFormatterSerialization (reading untrusted data is dangerous)

encoding-default.title: Encoding.Default (the default encoding)
encoding-default.note: .NET Framework's is the ANSI code page (Shift_JIS on a Japanese Windows), .NET's is UTF-8. Converter: replaced with Platform.DefaultEncoding

floating-point.title: Doubles and floats as text, and read from text
floating-point.note: Since .NET Core 3.0 a double without a format is the shortest text that round-trips (0.1 + 0.2 is 0.30000000000000004; .NET Framework: 15 digits, 0.3), negative zero is "-0", a fixed precision rounds the exact binary value to even (2.675 as N2 is 2.67; .NET Framework: 2.68, from its 15 digits). Parsing a number too large gives infinity (.NET Framework: an exception). TimeSpan.FromSeconds(0.00015) and the others are not rounded to milliseconds. Converter: replaced with FrameworkNumbers and FrameworkParsing (FOC1008, platformReplacements)

language-packs.title: .NET Framework language packs (System.Web's messages in Japanese and other languages)
language-packs.note: On a server with a language pack (ja on a Japanese Windows, usually) System.Web's texts are in its language when the UI culture is (Calendar's titles, Login's labels, Wizard's buttons, GridView's commands, error pages). .NET has no language packs. Converter: FrameworkOnCore's own translations (translations/) for the languages the original server had packs for (Microsoft's packs only when chosen and deployed on Windows only: their license forbids distributing them to run elsewhere). CultureInfo.DisplayName (.NET: in the language of Windows' UI) as mscorlib's and the packs' names (FrameworkCultures)

code-pages.title: Code pages (Shift_JIS and others)
code-pages.note: Without a registered provider .NET has only Unicode, ASCII and Latin-1. FrameworkOnCore's System.Web (UseWebForms) registers it at start

system-drawing.title: System.Drawing (images and fonts, GDI+)
system-drawing.note: .NET's System.Drawing.Common is Windows-only since .NET 7. Converter: FrameworkOnCore's System.Drawing.Common (a port with dotnet/runtime 6.0's Linux implementation, libgdiplus). What it draws (antialiasing, text) differs a little between Windows and Linux. Windows' fonts are not on Linux (Arial and others are replaced with compatible fonts)

charts.title: Charts (the Chart control)
charts.note: Ported from referencesource (MIT): package FrameworkOnCore.Web.DataVisualization (the Chart control, ChartImg.axd). Drawn with the ported System.Drawing (libgdiplus on Linux). When ChartImg.axd's image folder (appSettings ChartImageHandler's dir) is on C:, the deployment's setting (APPSETTING_ChartImageHandler) changes it on Linux. Windows Forms' System.Windows.Forms.DataVisualization is not ported

sql-client.title: SQL Server client (System.Data.SqlClient)
sql-client.note: .NET's System.Data.SqlClient rejects |DataDirectory| in connection strings (.NET Framework expanded it to App_Data). Converter: the port (FrameworkOnCore.Data.SqlClient) expands it as .NET Framework does

linq-to-sql.title: LINQ to SQL (System.Data.Linq)
linq-to-sql.note: Ported from referencesource (MIT): package FrameworkOnCore.Data.Linq (for SQL Server)

entity-framework-4.title: Entity Framework 4 (System.Data.Entity)
entity-framework-4.note: Converter: moved to EF6 (its package), the namespaces rewritten

wcf-data-services.title: WCF Data Services (OData client and server)

mobile-controls.title: Mobile controls (System.Web.Mobile)
mobile-controls.note: Deprecated in ASP.NET 4.0 (.NET Framework 4.8 has them). Ported from referencesource (MIT): package FrameworkOnCore.Web.Mobile

wcf-server.title: WCF services (ServiceHost, .svc)
wcf-server.note: .NET's WCF is the client only. Converter: run on CoreWCF (FrameworkOnCore.ServiceModel registers the .svc and web.config's services with CoreWCF)

wcf-client.title: WCF client (System.ServiceModel)
wcf-client.note: Converter: the System.ServiceModel.* packages (part of the client only)

windows-identity.title: Windows accounts and impersonation (WindowsIdentity)
windows-identity.note: Converter: Platform's replacements outside Windows (no account)

file-access-control.title: File and folder access control (ACLs)
file-access-control.note: Windows only. Converter: Directory/File.GetAccessControl and the others go to FrameworkOnCore.DirectoryAcl and FileAcl (they throw outside Windows)

registry.title: Registry (Microsoft.Win32.Registry)
registry.note: Outside Windows, Registry.LocalMachine and the others are null

oledb.title: OLE DB (reading Excel and Access files)
oledb.note: Windows only: Linux has no provider

directory-services.title: Active Directory (System.DirectoryServices)
directory-services.note: Windows only. Needs a rewrite to LDAP (System.DirectoryServices.Protocols)

code-access-security.title: Code access security (CAS)
code-access-security.note: .NET does nothing with it (there is no partial trust). Web applications usually run in full trust

remoting.title: Remoting (System.Runtime.Remoting)
remoting.note: Not in .NET. Some of it (CallContext) is in FrameworkOnCore's System.Web and the compatibility assembly

code-dom-compile.title: Compiling at run time (CodeDom)
code-dom-compile.note: .NET's CodeDom does not compile (it throws); it generates code only

web-request.title: WebRequest / WebClient
web-request.note: Obsolete in .NET but works (HttpClient is recommended)

legacy-crypto.title: Old cryptography classes (*CryptoServiceProvider, *Managed)
legacy-crypto.note: Obsolete in .NET but works (Rijndael's BlockSize 256 throws)

designers.title: Designers and Windows Forms
designers.note: For Visual Studio's designers. Converter: stubbed, removed from web.config

web-forms.title: ASP.NET (System.Web: Web Forms, ASMX)
web-forms.note: FrameworkOnCore (System.Web and the others, from WebFormsForCore) has them for .NET

visual-basic-runtime.title: Visual Basic runtime (Microsoft.VisualBasic)
visual-basic-runtime.note: .NET's Microsoft.VisualBasic.Core. Some of My's types are in the compatibility assembly

dll-references.title: DLL references without their types
dll-references.note: A DLL without source references a type as "assembly + type"; these are types .NET 10 has in another assembly (which ones: APIs; each API is counted in its own component too)
